```plato

//==
// # The linear system and its solution
//
// The assembled system is a `SparseMatrix` (`matrices.types.plato`) in
// coordinate-list form, and it is solved by a preconditioned conjugate gradient
// that never indexes it. See the library's "Assembly" section for why those two
// choices belong together.

// When a conjugate-gradient solve stops: after MaxIterations sweeps, or once the
// residual norm has fallen to Tolerance times its starting value, whichever
// comes first. Tolerance is a RELATIVE residual, so it is independent of the
// units the loads are stated in.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjugate_gradient_method)
type LinearSolveSettings
    implements IValue
{
    MaxIterations: Integer;
    Tolerance: Number;
}

// What a solve of the constrained system returned. Converged reports whether the
// residual reached the requested tolerance; Solution holds the last iterate
// either way, so a caller that ignores the flag gets a partially converged
// answer rather than nothing.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Partial operations (a concrete result record
// with a validity field).
type LinearSolveResult
    implements IValue
{
    Solution: Array<Number>;
    Iterations: Integer;
    Residual: Number;
    Converged: Boolean;
}

//==
// # Analysis results
//
// Per-node displacement, in the same order as the mesh positions, plus the
// convergence report of the solve that produced it. Element strain, element
// stress and von Mises stress are DERIVED from a solution rather than stored in
// it — see the library's "Recovering strain and stress" section.

// The displaced state of a solid model: one displacement vector per mesh
// position, in meters.
type ElasticSolution3D
    implements IValue
{
    Displacements: Array<Vector3D>;
    Iterations: Integer;
    Residual: Number;
    Converged: Boolean;
}

// The displaced state of a plane model: one in-plane displacement vector per
// mesh position, in meters.
type ElasticSolution2D
    implements IValue
{
    Displacements: Array<Vector2D>;
    Iterations: Integer;
    Residual: Number;
    Converged: Boolean;
}

// The displaced state of a beam discretised into uniform elements. Positions
// holds the node stations measured from the beam's start; Deflections and
// Rotations hold the two degrees of freedom at each of them, in meters and in
// radians. Deflection is positive in the direction transverse loads are positive
// (downward), matching `BeamLoad` in `engineering.types.plato`.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler%E2%80%93Bernoulli_beam_theory)
type BeamSolution
    implements IValue
{
    Positions: Array<Length>;
    Deflections: Array<Number>;
    Rotations: Array<Number>;
    Iterations: Integer;
    Residual: Number;
    Converged: Boolean;
}
```
